title: Salvianic acid A alleviates hepatic fibrosis by inhibiting the AKT1/NF-kappaB axis.
authors: Hu, Jinqi; Zhang, Jiexin; Ge, Xiaomei; Li, Suyu; Li, Xudong; Zhang, Tianrui; Li, Xiang; He, Meng; Gao, Guanbin; Sun, Taolei
one_liner_zh: 该文研究丹参素A通过抑制AKT1/NF-kB轴缓解肝纤维化，虽用分子对接和MD模拟，但对象为蛋白-小分子互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Hepatic fibrosis (HF) is a crucial and reversible stage, yet there is a paucity of effective clinical antifibrotic drugs. Salvianic acid A (SAA) has shown antifibrotic potential in preliminary studies; however, its molecular mechanisms and potential targets remain incompletely understood. To evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and mechanisms of SAA in mitigating HF, we employed a carbon tetrachloride (CCl(4))-induced HF mouse model. In parallel, we used transforming growth factor beta 1 (TGF-beta1)-stimulated LX-2 cells and primary mouse hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) for in vitro studies. In CCl(4)-induced mice, SAA markedly improved liver function and suppressed HF, as evidenced by significant reduction in alpha-smooth muscle actin and collagen I expression and alleviation of inflammatory response. Similar antifibrotic and anti-inflammatory effects were observed in vitro. To investigate the targets and mechanism of SAA in HF, we employed network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, and microscale thermophoresis. We found that SAA was predicted to interact with the allosteric pocket of RAC-alpha serine/threonine-protein kinase 1 (AKT1), accompanied by inhibition of AKT1 phosphorylation and the downstream nuclear factor-kappa B (NF-kappaB) signaling. To further explore the involvement of AKT1 in SAA's antifibrotic effects, we used the AKT activator SC79. In CCl(4)-induced mice, SC79 partly reversed the antifibrotic effects of SAA. Consistently, we observed that SC79 partially restored the inflammatory and fibrotic markers in TGF-beta1-simulated HSCs, counteracting the inhibitory efficacy of SAA. Our findings suggest that SAA exerts antifibrotic effects in part through suppression of the AKT1/NF-kappaB axis and may represent a promising therapeutic candidate for HF.
abstract_zh: 肝纤维化（HF）是一个关键且可逆的阶段，然而目前缺乏有效的临床抗纤维化药物。丹酚酸A（SAA）在初步研究中显示出抗纤维化潜力；然而，其分子机制和潜在靶点仍未完全阐明。为评估SAA在缓解HF中的治疗效果及机制，我们采用了四氯化碳（CCl(4)）诱导的HF小鼠模型。同时，我们使用转化生长因子β1（TGF-beta1）刺激的LX-2细胞和小鼠原代肝星状细胞（HSCs）进行体外研究。在CCl(4)诱导的小鼠中，SAA显著改善了肝功能并抑制了HF，表现为α-平滑肌肌动蛋白和胶原I表达显著降低，以及炎症反应减轻。体外实验中也观察到类似的抗纤维化和抗炎效果。为探究SAA在HF中的靶点和机制，我们采用了网络药理学、分子对接、分子动力学模拟和微量热泳动技术。我们发现SAA被预测与RAC-α丝氨酸/苏氨酸蛋白激酶1（AKT1）的变构口袋相互作用，并伴随AKT1磷酸化及其下游核因子-κB（NF-kappaB）信号的抑制。为进一步探讨AKT1在SAA抗纤维化作用中的参与，我们使用了AKT激活剂SC79。在CCl(4)诱导的小鼠中，SC79部分逆转了SAA的抗纤维化效果。一致地，我们观察到SC79在TGF-beta1刺激的HSCs中部分恢复了炎症和纤维化标志物，抵消了SAA的抑制功效。我们的研究结果表明，SAA部分通过抑制AKT1/NF-kappaB轴发挥抗纤维化作用，并可能成为HF的有前景的治疗候选药物。
